findings.title: The hostile-at check proves no markup reaches the DOM but never exercises esc(), and its label says it did, so L-4's rendered-through-esc clause stays unpinned

evidence.value: const hostile = the ISO time with an img/onerror fragment appended; e.fire(...); assert.equal(asOf().innerHTML, ''); assert.doesNotMatch(asOf().innerHTML, /<img|onerror/i); then ok('... rendered through esc(), no HTML injected, no console error')

A scratch copy of site/index.html with esc() removed from the asOf line only - esc(when(lastRefresh.at)) changed to when(lastRefresh.at) - passes all 96 page checks (PAGE_HTML pointed at the copy, exit 0). The hostile string is rejected one step earlier, by new Date() returning Invalid Date, so it never reaches esc().

site/index.html:271 - when = iso => { const d = new Date(iso); return isNaN(d) ? '' : d.toLocaleString(...); }. Any at that renders must have parsed as a date, and what reaches innerHTML is toLocaleString output, never the input, so esc() on that line is defence in depth no input can exercise.
PBI-008 L-4: the time comes from at, rendered through esc(); each case is pinned by a page check.

findings.impact: The property L-4 actually cares about - no fragment of a hostile at reaching the DOM - is pinned, and it holds for a stronger reason than the check states: when() launders every value through toLocaleString, so injection here is impossible by construction, not merely escaped. Nothing wrong would ship. Two small residues remain: the ok() label asserts the value was rendered through esc() when the run never enters esc(), so the suite's own report overstates what it proved; and a future edit dropping esc() from that line would go unnoticed. Both are cosmetic while when() stands between at and the DOM, which is why this is LOW and not the MEDIUM it inherited from CR-1.
findings.remediation: Reword the ok() label and the comment above it to state what the run proves - a hostile at fails to parse and renders nothing, so no fragment can reach the DOM - instead of claiming esc() ran. If the esc() clause is ever to be pinned mechanically, the only honest way is a direct check on esc() itself, since no at value can carry markup past when(). Neither change is required for merge.

not_audited.ref: A literal round-1 versus round-2 file diff
not_audited.reason: The change is uncommitted and no round-1 snapshot was kept, so a literal r1-to-r2 diff was impossible; weakening was ruled out indirectly instead, and the evidence is conclusive. git numstat against base d10d9e6 shows tests/page.test.mjs 76 insertions and 0 deletions and site/index.html 18 insertions and 0 deletions, so no pre-existing line was removed from either. Every assertion findings-r1.json quotes verbatim is still present, the five round-1 ok() labels are all still among the seven now in page check 19 (94 to 96 checks equals the two added), and the two places that changed both gained assertions: the corrupt-at case went from one value to a six-value class, and the 5-minute case gained an exact-equality check beside its prefix match. The 30 deleted lines in tests/test_refresh.py and the 9 in exporters/refresh.py were read one by one: they are round-1 count updates, this round's two renames, and the deleted nothing-to-push branch, each replaced by an equal-or-stronger assertion.

No browser: the page checks run against a stub DOM, so .faint.stale resolving to var(--changes) and never var(--human) was verified by reading the CSS (site/index.html:37, where .faint.stale at specificity 0,2,0 beats .faint at 0,1,0) and asserted by class name in the checks, not rendered.

No Touchstone SARIF and no SAST in this repo, so code-level security is reasoning-only. Re-reviewed this round and clean: the one new externally visible value is lastRefresh.at, which cannot reach the DOM as markup because when() returns either the empty string or toLocaleString output; the new type guard closes the malformed-input class (null, 0, true, a number, an object, a bad string - all now silent, all pinned); there is no new secret, deserialization, path, command or authz surface; the store's write rule is admin-only and unchanged.

follow_ups.note: Carried from round 1 and now firmer - see finding CR-6. CLAUDE.md's refresh procedure (line 54) still says refresh.py prints nothing to push if none, and the /loop instruction (line 73) still guards on that string; PRD FR-46 (line 306) still requires it, and FR-46 and FR-52 cite renamed tests. Both files are outside this PBI's allowed_areas and the PBI defers them by design, so the chore should land with or immediately after the merge, and should also add a meta/lastRefresh row to CLAUDE.md's store-path table.

follow_ups.ref: tests/page.test.mjs - the exact-match check duplicates the page's date-format options
follow_ups.note: The new check builds its expected string with its own toLocaleString options object, copied from when() at site/index.html:271. That duplication is what makes the check exact and is the right trade, but a future cosmetic change to when()'s options will fail it for a formatting reason rather than a behavioural one. Worth a one-line comment pointing at when() so the next reader knows where to update it.
